about: Delivery presets for --target <name>: canvas size and fps (design pixels), and the safe rectangle where text and key objects belong (x, y, w, h from the top-left). Each edge of the rectangle has its own record in `edges`: where it is (`at`, in design pixels), its `source`, the date it was `measured` (null until it is), and `estimate`. A target may also list `exclude`: rectangles inside `safe` that the platform covers anyway (TikTok's action-button column), each { x, y, w, h, source }; text that overlaps one counts as outside the safe area, and the --safe overlays shade it. A target is an estimate while any of its edges is, and then render.mjs check reports text outside it as WARN rather than FAIL, and the --safe overlays say "estimate". The *-ad targets are the platforms' published safe zones for 9:16 ads, measured from their sources; they are stricter than organic posts. The organic targets (tiktok, reels, shorts) are researched estimates: no platform publishes an organic zone, so their edges come from published third-party measurements, cited with the research date. CFG.W, CFG.H and CFG.FPS in a scene win over these.
method: How the numbers are set (plan Q3). The ad targets (*-ad) are measured from each platform's published safe-zone template or spec, scaled to the canvas, each edge citing its source, with estimate false. No platform publishes an organic zone, so the organic targets (tiktok, reels, shorts) take each edge from published third-party measurements of the app's UI, compared and cited, with the research date in its source; where they disagree, the more conservative figure, unless a source shows why it differs. They keep estimate true and measured null, because the overlays move with the device and with the caption's length, so render.mjs check reports text outside them as WARN, never FAIL. An area the app covers inside the rectangle (a column of buttons) goes in exclude. To refine an edge from an in-app screenshot, scale it so the video is 1080 px wide and record the first row or column no overlay covers; grid.js, a labelled grid, can help read positions off it.

tiktok.source: Researched 2026-11-14 from published third-party measurements of the organic TikTok UI (cadenus.io, vidova.ai): 44 left, 130 top, a 140-wide button rail on the right, and 484 at the bottom for the username, caption and sound rows. TikTok publishes only its ad zone (tiktok-ad). An estimate: the overlays move with the device and with the caption's length.

bottom.source: 484 px for the username, caption and sound rows (cadenus.io; 480-484 elsewhere; vidova gives 320). It matches TikTok's own In-Feed ad template's 660 px bottom less the ad's call-to-action and sponsored label. It grows with longer captions. Researched 2026-11-14
